value.zh: 南土越崔巂民夷聞嶷死，無不悲泣，為嶷立廟，四時水旱輒祀之。
value.en: Southern Han and Yi of Yuexi wept at Zhang Ni’s death, built him shrines, and prayed there whenever drought or flood struck.
value.literal: People of the southern lands—the Han and Yi of Yuexi Commandery—hearing of Ni's death, none did not weep in sorrow; they erected a temple for Ni; at the four seasons for flood or drought they always sacrificed to him.

value.zh: 〈《益部耆舊傳》曰：余觀張嶷儀貌辭令，不能駭人，而其策略足以入算，果烈足以立威，為臣有忠誠之節，處類有亮直之風，而動必顧典，後主深崇之。
value.en: 〈The Yibu tradition says Zhang Ni looked unremarkable yet planned brilliantly, fought fiercely, served with steadfast loyalty, stood candid among colleagues, and weighed every act against precedent—so Liu Shan revered him deeply.
value.literal: 〈The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: I observed Zhang Ni—his bearing and speech could not startle people, yet his stratagems sufficed to enter calculation; his decisive fierceness sufficed to establish awe; as minister he had integrity of loyalty; among peers he had the wind of candid straightness; yet in action he always consulted the canon—the Later Lord deeply revered him.

value.zh: 雖古之英士，何以遠逾哉！
value.en: Ancient heroes would scarcely surpass him!
value.literal: Although compared to ancient heroic gentlemen—how could they surpass him far!

value.zh: 《蜀世譜》曰：嶷孫奕，晉梁州刺史。〉
value.en: The Shu shifu adds that Zhang Ni’s grandson Zhang Yi became Jin’s inspector of Liangzhou.〉
value.literal: The Shu Shifu states: Ni's grandson Yi was Liang Province Inspector of Jin.〉

value.zh: 馬忠字德信，巴西閬中人也。
value.en: Ma Zhong, styled Dexin, came from Langzhong in Ba-Xi Commandery.
value.literal: Ma Zhong, courtesy name Dexin, was a man of Langzhong in Ba-Xi.

value.zh: 少養外家，姓狐，名篤，後乃復姓，改名忠。
value.en: Raised in his mother's Hu clan under the name Du, he later resumed the surname Ma and took the name Zhong.
value.literal: In youth he was raised by his maternal family, surnamed Hu and named Du; later he restored his surname and changed his name to Zhong.

value.zh: 為郡吏，建安末舉孝廉，除漢昌長。
value.en: He served as a commandery clerk and, at the end of Jian'an, was recommended as filial and incorrupt and made chief of Hanchang.
value.literal: He was a commandery clerk; at the end of the Jian'an era he was recommended as filial and incorrupt and appointed chief of Hanchang.

value.zh: 先主東征，敗績猇亭，巴西太守閻芝發諸縣兵五千人以補遣闕，遣忠送往。
value.en: After Liu Bei's defeat at Xiaoting, Ba-Xi administrator Yan Zhi raised five thousand county troops to fill the army's losses and sent Ma Zhong with them.
value.literal: When the First Sovereign campaigned east and was defeated at Xiaoting, Ba-Xi Administrator Yan Zhi mobilized five thousand troops from the various counties to fill shortages and losses and sent Zhong to deliver them.

value.zh: 先主已還永安，見忠與語，謂尚書令劉巴曰：「雖亡黃權，復得狐篤，此為世不乏賢也。」
value.en: Liu Bei had already returned to Yong'an. After meeting Ma Zhong he told Masters-of-Writing Director Liu Ba, "Though I lost Huang Quan, I have gained Hu Du—the world never lacks talent."
value.literal: The First Sovereign had already returned to Yong'an. Seeing Zhong and speaking with him, he said to Masters-of-Writing Director Liu Ba: "Though I have lost Huang Quan, I have again gained Hu Du—this shows the age is never short of worthy men."

value.zh: 建興元年223年，丞相亮開府，以忠為下督。
value.en: In Jianxing 1 Zhuge Liang opened his chancellor's bureau and named Ma Zhong lower supervisor.
value.literal: In the first year of Jianxing [223], Chancellor Liang opened his bureau and appointed Zhong lower supervisor.

value.zh: 三年，亮入南，拜忠牂牁太守。
value.en: In Jianxing 3, when Zhuge Liang marched south, he made Ma Zhong administrator of Zangke.
value.literal: In the third year, when Liang entered the south, he appointed Zhong Administrator of Zangke.

value.zh: 郡丞朱褒反。
value.en: Assistant administrator Zhu Bao rebelled.
value.literal: Assistant Administrator Zhu Bao rebelled.

value.zh: 叛亂之後，忠撫育卹理，甚有威惠。
value.en: After the rebellion Ma Zhong nursed the people back to order with both sternness and kindness.
value.literal: After the rebellion, Zhong nurtured and comforted the people and governed them; he had great authority and grace.

value.zh: 八年，召為丞相參軍，副長史蔣琬署留府事。
value.en: In Jianxing 8 he was recalled as the chancellor's army adviser, assisting chief clerk Jiang Wan in running the rear headquarters.
value.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned as army adviser to the chancellor, assisting Chief Clerk Jiang Wan in administering rear headquarters affairs.

value.zh: 又領州治中從事。
value.en: He also served concurrently as director of the provincial headquarters staff.
value.literal: He also concurrently served as director of the headquarters staff of the province.

value.zh: 明年，亮出祁山，忠詣亮所，經營戌事。
value.en: The next year, when Zhuge Liang marched to Qishan, Ma Zhong joined his headquarters to manage garrison affairs.
value.literal: The next year, when Liang marched out to Qishan, Zhong went to Liang's headquarters and managed garrison affairs.

value.zh: 軍還，督將軍張嶷等討汶山郡叛羌。
value.en: After the campaign he directed Zhang Ni and others against rebel Qiang in Wenshan Commandery.
value.literal: When the army returned, he supervised Generals Zhang Ni and others in punishing the rebel Qiang of Wenshan Commandery.

value.zh: 十一年，南夷豪帥劉冑反，擾亂諸郡。
value.en: In Jianxing 11 the southern chieftain Liu Zhou rebelled and threw several commanderies into turmoil.
value.literal: In the eleventh year the southern Yi chieftain Liu Zhou rebelled and disturbed the various commanderies.

value.zh: 徵庲降都督張冀還，以忠代冀。
value.en: Laixiang area commander Zhang Ji was recalled and Ma Zhong replaced him.
value.literal: Area Commander of Laixiang Zhang Ji was recalled and Zhong replaced Ji.

value.zh: 忠遂斬冑，平南土。
value.en: Ma Zhong beheaded Liu Zhou and pacified the south.
value.literal: Zhong thereupon beheaded Zhou and pacified the southern lands.

value.zh: 加忠監軍、奮威將軍，封博陽亭侯。
value.en: He was promoted to army supervisor and general who displays might and enfeoffed as village marquis of Boyang.
value.literal: Zhong was additionally made army supervisor and General Who Displays Might, and enfeoffed as village marquis of Boyang.

value.zh: 初，建寧郡殺太守正昂，縛太守張裔於吳，故都督常駐平夷縣。
value.en: Earlier Jianning had killed Administrator Zheng Ang and sent Administrator Zhang Yi bound to Wu, so area commanders had long been stationed at Pingyi County.
value.literal: At first Jianning Commandery killed Administrator Zheng Ang and bound Administrator Zhang Yi in Wu; therefore area commanders had regularly been stationed at Pingyi County.

value.zh: 至忠，乃移治味縣，處民夷之間。
value.en: Under Ma Zhong the seat moved to Wei County, among Han and tribal settlements.
value.literal: When Zhong took office, he moved the seat to Wei County, placing it among Han and tribal peoples.

value.zh: 又越嶲郡亦久失土地，忠率將太守張嶷開复舊郡，由此就加安南將軍，進封彭鄉亭侯。
value.en: He also led Zhang Ni to recover long-lost Yuexi territory and was promoted to general who pacifies the south and advanced to village marquis of Pengxiang.
value.literal: Moreover Yuexi Commandery had long lost territory; Zhong led Administrator Zhang Ni to reopen and recover the old commandery; thereby he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and advanced to village marquis of Pengxiang.

value.zh: 延熙五年還朝，因至漢中，見大司馬蔣琬，宣傳詔旨，加拜鎮南大將軍。
value.en: In Yanxi 5 he returned to court, stopped at Hanzhong to see Grand Marshal Jiang Wan, delivered the imperial edict, and was promoted to grand general who guards the south.
value.literal: In the fifth year of Yanxi he returned to court, and on the way to Hanzhong he saw Grand Marshal Jiang Wan, proclaimed the imperial edict, and was additionally appointed Grand General Who Guards the South.

value.zh: 七年春，大將軍費韋北禦魏敵，留忠成都，平尚書事。
value.en: In the spring of Yanxi 7 Grand General Fei Yi marched north against Wei and left Ma Zhong at Chengdu to balance masters-of-writing affairs.
value.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, Grand General Fei Yi marched north to resist Wei enemies and left Zhong at Chengdu to balance Masters-of-Writing affairs.

value.zh: 禕還，忠乃歸南。
value.en: When Fei Yi returned, Ma Zhong went back south.
value.literal: When Yi returned, Zhong then returned south.

value.zh: 十二年卒，子脩嗣。
value.en: He died in the twelfth year [of Yanxi]; his son Ma Xiu inherited the title.
value.literal: In the twelfth year [of Yanxi] he died; his son Xiu succeeded.

value.zh: 脩弟恢。
value.en: Ma Xiu's younger brother was Hui.
value.literal: Xiu's younger brother was Hui.

value.zh: 恢子義，晉建寧太守。
value.en: Hui's son Yi served Jin as administrator of Jianning.
value.literal: Hui's son Yi was Administrator of Jianning under Jin.

value.zh: 忠為人寬濟有度量，但恢啁大笑，忿怒不形於色。
value.en: Ma Zhong was generous and broad-minded, laughed loudly when pleased, and never let anger show.
value.literal: Zhong as a man was generous and relieving, with breadth of measure; only when cheerful he laughed loudly, and anger did not show on his face.

value.zh: 然處事能斷，威思並立，是以蠻夷畏而愛之。
value.en: Yet he decided firmly, pairing authority with kindness, so the tribes both feared and loved him.
value.literal: Yet in handling affairs he could decide; authority and kindness stood together—therefore the tribes both feared and loved him.

value.zh: 及卒，莫不自致喪庭，流涕盡哀，為之立廟祀，迄今猶在。
value.en: At his death tribesmen came in person to mourn, weeping fully, and built shrines to him that still stand.
value.literal: When he died, none failed to come in person to the mourning hall, weeping with full grief; they built temples to sacrifice to him, which remain to this day.

value.zh: 張表，時名士，清望逾忠。
value.en: Zhang Biao was a celebrated gentleman whose repute outshone Ma Zhong's.
value.literal: Zhang Biao was a famed gentleman of the time; his pure reputation surpassed Zhong's.

value.zh: 閻宇宿有功幹，於事精勤。
value.en: Yan Yu had long shown ability and handled affairs with care.
value.literal: Yan Yu for long had merit and capability and was meticulous and diligent in affairs.

value.zh: 繼踵在忠後，其威風稱績，皆不及忠。
value.en: Successors who followed Ma Zhong never matched his authority or record.
value.literal: Those who followed in Zhong's footsteps—their authority, reputation, and achievements all did not reach Zhong's.

value.zh: 《益部耆舊傳》曰：張表，肅子也。
value.en: The Yibu tradition says Zhang Biao was Su's son.
value.literal: The Traditions of Former Worthies of Yibu states: Zhang Biao was the son of Su.

value.zh: 《華陽國志》云：表，張松子，未詳。
value.en: The Huayang guo zhi says Biao was the son of Zhang Song—this is uncertain.
value.literal: The Huayang guo zhi says: Biao was Zhang Songzi—uncertain.

value.zh: 閻宇字文平，南郡人也。
value.en: Yan Yu, styled Wenping, came from Nan Commandery.
value.literal: Yan Yu, courtesy name Wenping, was a man of Nan Commandery.

value.zh: 蔣琬字公琰，零陵湘鄉人也。
value.en: Jiang Wan, courtesy name Gongyan, came from Xiangxiang in Lingling Commandery.
value.literal: Jiang Wan, courtesy name Gongyan, was a native of Xiangxiang in Lingling.

value.zh: 弱冠與外弟泉陵劉敏懼知名。
value.en: While still young he won local fame alongside his cousin Liu Min of Quanling.
value.literal: While still young he won local fame alongside his cousin Liu Min of Quanling.

value.zh: 琬以州書佐隨先主入蜀，除廣都長。
value.en: He entered Shu as a provincial clerk under Liu Bei and was named magistrate of Guangdu.
value.literal: Wan served as a provincial clerk and followed the Vanguard Lord into Shu; he was appointed magistrate of Guangdu.

value.zh: 先主嘗因遊觀奄至廣都，見琬眾事不理，時又沉醉，先主大怒，將加罪戮。
value.en: Liu Bei came to Guangdu on a tour, found Jiang Wan drunk and neglecting his duties, and was ready to execute him.
value.literal: The Vanguard Lord once on a pleasure outing suddenly arrived at Guangdu and saw Wan leaving official business unattended and at the time also deeply drunk; the Vanguard Lord was greatly angry and was about to impose punishment and execution.

value.zh: 軍師將軍諸葛亮請曰：「蔣琬，社稷之器，非百里之才也。
value.en: Zhuge Liang intervened: "Jiang Wan is material for the empire, not a petty county magistrate.
value.literal: Army commander Zhuge Liang pleaded, saying, "Jiang Wan is vessel of the altars of soil and grain—not talent for a hundred li.

value.zh: 其為政以安民為本，不以修飾為先，願主公重加察之。」
value.en: He rules by putting the people at ease, not by polished appearances—please look again, my lord."
value.literal: His governing takes pacifying the people as root, not ornament as first; wish the lord examine him again carefully."

value.zh: 先主雅敬亮，乃不加罪，倉卒但免官而已。
value.en: Liu Bei yielded to Zhuge Liang and spared him—stripping him of office alone.
value.literal: The Vanguard Lord always respected Liang and therefore did not add punishment; in haste he only dismissed from office.

value.zh: 琬見推之後，夜夢有—牛頭在門前，流血滂沱，意甚惡之，呼問占夢趙直。
value.en: After his promotion Jiang Wan dreamed of a bloody ox head at his gate and consulted Zhao Zhi about it.
value.literal: After Wan was promoted, he dreamed at night of an ox head before the gate, bleeding profusely—his intent felt very ill; he called to ask dream-diviner Zhao Zhi.

value.zh: 直曰：「夫見血者，事分明也。
value.en: Zhi said, "Seeing blood means affairs are clear-cut.
value.literal: Zhi said, "Seeing blood means affairs are clear-cut.

value.zh: 牛角及鼻，『公』字之象，君位必當至公，大吉之征也。」
value.en: Horns and snout sketch the word ‘duke’—you are destined for high, impartial office; most auspicious."
value.literal: Ox horn and nose are images of the character ‘public’; your position must reach utmost fairness—a greatly auspicious sign."

value.zh: 頃之，為什邡令。
value.en: Soon he was appointed magistrate of Shifang.
value.literal: Shortly thereafter he became magistrate of Shifang.

value.zh: 先主為漢中王，琬人為尚書郎。
value.en: When Liu Bei took the title King of Hanzhong, Jiang Wan became a secretary in the imperial secretariat.
value.literal: When the Vanguard Lord became King of Hanzhong, Wan entered as gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

value.zh: 姜維，字伯約，天水冀人也。
value.en: Jiang Wei, courtesy name Boyue, came from Ji in Tianshui.
value.literal: Jiang Wei, courtesy name Boyue, was a man of Ji in Tianshui.

value.zh: 少孤，與母居，好鄭氏學。
value.en: Orphaned young, he lived with his mother and studied Zheng Xuan’s classical scholarship.
value.literal: In youth orphaned, he dwelt with his mother and loved Zheng Xuan's learning.

value.zh: 〈《傅子》曰：维为人好立功名，阴养死士，不脩布衣之业。〉
value.en: < Fu Xuan claims Jiang Wei schemed for glory and kept a retinue of fighting men.>
value.literal: < The Fu Zi says: Wei by nature loved to establish merit and fame; secretly he nurtured braves and did not cultivate commoner's occupation.>

value.zh: 仕郡上計掾，州闢為從事。
value.en: He rose to county accountant and then provincial attendant.
value.literal: He served the commandery as accounts clerk; the province summoned him as attendant clerk.

value.zh: 以父冏昔為郡功曹，值羌、戎叛亂，身衛郡將，沒於戰場，賜維官中郎，參本郡軍事。
value.en: His father Jiang Jiong died defending the prefect against Qiang rebels; Jiang Wei received a cadet’s rank and a place on the staff.
value.literal: Because father Jiong long ago was commandery merit clerk—when Qiang and Rong rebelled he guarded the prefect and died on the battlefield—Wei was granted gentleman cadet and joined his commandery's military staff.

value.zh: 建興六年，丞相諸葛亮軍向祁山，時天水太守適出案行。
value.en: In 228 Zhuge Liang marched on Qi—Tianshui’s prefect was away on circuit.
value.literal: In Jianxing's sixth year Chancellor Zhuge Liang's army aimed at Mount Qi—at that time Tianshui's prefect happened to be out inspecting.

value.zh: 維及功曹梁緒、主簿尹賞、主記梁虔等從行。
value.en: Jiang Wei rode with Liang Xu, Yin Shang, Liang Qian, and the staff.
value.literal: Wei together with merit clerk Liang Xu, chief clerk Yin Shang, recorder Liang Qian and others followed the circuit.

value.zh: 太守聞蜀軍垂至而諸縣響應，疑維等皆有異心，於是夜亡保上邽。
value.en: The prefect feared collaboration with Shu and fled overnight to Shanggui.
value.literal: The prefect heard Shu troops were near and counties were responding—suspected Wei and others all had alien hearts—thereupon fled by night to hold Shanggui.

value.zh: 維等覺太守去，追遲，至城門，城門已閉，不納。
value.en: They caught up too late; the city gates shut them out.
value.literal: Wei and others noticed the prefect had gone—pursued late—reached the gate—the gate was closed—not admitted.

value.zh: 維等相率還冀，冀亦不入維。
value.en: They rode to Ji, but Ji refused them too.
value.literal: Wei and others led one another back to Ji—Ji also would not admit Wei.

value.zh: 維等乃俱詣諸葛亮。
value.en: They went together to Zhuge Liang.
value.literal: Wei and others then all went to Zhuge Liang.

value.zh: 會馬謖敗於街亭。
value.en: Ma Su had just been crushed at Jieting.
value.literal: It happened Ma Su was defeated at Jieting.

value.zh: 亮拔將西縣千餘家及維等還，故維遂與母相失。
value.en: Zhuge Liang evacuated Xixian and brought Jiang Wei along—parting him from his mother.
value.literal: Liang pulled west county thousand-plus households and Wei and others back—therefore Wei then lost contact with his mother.

value.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：天水太守马遵将维及诸官属随雍州刺史郭淮偶自西至洛门案行，会闻亮已到祁山，淮顾遵曰：“是欲不善！”
value.en: < The Wei Lue adds another flight from Tianshui: Ma Zun was west of Luomen with Guo Huai when news of Zhuge Liang arrived—Guo Huai cried trouble.
value.literal: < The Wei Lue says: Tianshui prefect Ma Zun led Wei and officials following provincial governor Guo Huai on circuit west to Luomen—happened to hear Liang had reached Qi Mountain—Huai looked at Zun and said, "This cannot be good!

value.zh: 遂驱东还上邽。
value.en: They galloped back toward Shanggui.
value.literal: Thereupon drove east back to Shanggui.

value.zh: 遵念所治冀县界在西偏，又恐吏民乐乱，遂亦随淮去。
value.en: Ma Zun feared unrest in his western districts and fled with Guo Huai.
value.literal: Zun thought his jurisdiction Ji County lay on the west flank—also feared officials and people would delight in chaos—thereupon also followed Huai away.

value.zh: 时维谓遵曰：“明府当还冀。”
value.en: Jiang Wei urged Ma Zun to return and hold Ji.
value.literal: At the time Wei said to Zun, "My lord ought to return to Ji.

value.zh: 遵谓维等曰：“卿诸人
value.en: Ma Zun told them, "You people—
value.literal: Zun said to Wei and others, "You gentlemen—

value.en: (text breaks mid-clause)
value.literal: (return)

value.zh: 复信，皆贼也。”
value.en: —if you defect to the enemy you are traitors every one."
value.literal: if you turn back again—all are bandits."

value.zh: 各自行。
value.en: Then each rode his separate path.
value.literal: Each went his own way.

value.zh: 维亦无如遵何，而家在冀，遂与郡吏上官子脩等还冀。
value.en: Powerless to sway Ma Zun, Jiang Wei headed home to Ji with staff officer Shangguan Zixiu.
value.literal: Wei could do nothing about Zun—but his home was in Ji—thereupon with county clerk Shangguan Zixiu and others returned to Ji.

value.zh: 冀中吏民见维等大喜，便推令见亮。
value.en: The people of Ji welcomed them and urged them to meet Zhuge Liang.
value.literal: Ji officials and people seeing Wei and others greatly rejoiced—and pushed them to go see Liang.

value.zh: 二人不获已，乃共诣亮。
value.en: With little choice both men presented themselves to Zhuge Liang.
value.literal: The two could not avoid it—thereupon together went to Liang.

value.zh: 亮见，大悦。
value.en: Zhuge Liang received them gladly.
value.literal: Liang seeing them greatly rejoiced.

value.zh: 未及遣迎冀中人，会亮前锋为张郃、费繇等所破，遂将维等卻缩。
value.en: Before Ji could be secured the vanguard fell to Zhang He—Zhuge Liang had to pull Jiang Wei back.
value.literal: Before he could dispatch to welcome Ji people—it happened Liang's vanguard was broken by Zhang He, Fei Yao and others—thereupon led Wei and others to shrink back.

value.zh: 维不得还，遂入蜀。
value.en: Cut off from Wei, Jiang Wei entered Shu.
value.literal: Wei could not return—thereupon entered Shu.

value.zh: 诸军攻冀，皆得维母妻子，亦以维本无去意，故不没其家，但系保官以延之。
value.en: Wei besieged Ji and took his family but did not execute them, hoping to lure him back.
value.literal: The various armies attacked Ji—all obtained Wei's mother and wife—also because Wei originally had no intent to leave—therefore did not confiscate his family—but tied them in protective custody to entice him.

value.zh: 此语与本傳不同。
value.en: This variant differs from the standard account.>
value.literal: This language differs from the main biography.>

value.zh: 亮辟維為倉曹掾，加奉義將軍，封當陽亭侯，時年二十七。
value.en: Zhuge Liang made him Granary Clerk, General Who Upholds Righteousness, and Village Marquis of Dangyang—at twenty-seven.
value.literal: Liang summoned Wei as granary clerk; added general who upholds righteousness; enfeoffed village marquis of Dangyang—at the time age twenty-seven.

value.zh: 亮與留府長史張裔、參軍蔣琬書曰：「姜伯約忠勤時事，思慮精密，考其所有，永南、季常諸人不如也。
value.en: He wrote Zhang Yi and Jiang Wan: "Jiang Wei is meticulous and loyal—Yongnan and Jichang cannot compare.
value.literal: Liang wrote to chief clerk Zhang Yi and adviser Jiang Wan: "Jiang Boyue is loyal and diligent in affairs of the time—thought careful and fine—measuring his qualities—Yongnan and Jichang and such do not match.

value.zh: 其人，涼州上士也。」
value.en: He is the finest talent of the northwest."
value.literal: This man is upper gentry of Liangzhou."

value.zh: 又曰：「須先教中虎步兵五六千人。
value.en: Also said: "Must first drill central tiger infantry five or six thousand.
value.literal: Also said: "Must first drill central tiger infantry five or six thousand.

value.zh: 姜伯約甚敏於軍事，既有膽義，深解兵意。
value.en: He is bold in war and grasps how soldiers think.
value.literal: Jiang Boyue is very keen in military affairs—already has courage and duty—deeply understands soldier intent.

value.zh: 此人心存漢室而才兼於人，畢教軍事，當遣詣宮，覲見主上。」
value.en: His heart is Han’s—once trained, bring him to audience."
value.literal: This man's heart cherishes the House of Han while talent surpasses others—when military teaching is finished—ought send him to palace—to gaze on the lord."

value.zh: 〈孙盛杂记曰：初，姜维诣亮，与母相失，复得母书，令求当归。
value.en: < Sun Sheng adds that his mother wrote demanding he return.
value.literal: < Sun Sheng's Miscellany says: At first when Jiang Wei went to Liang he lost his mother—again obtained mother's letter ordering him to seek danggui medicine.

value.zh: 维曰：“良田百顷，不在一亩，但有远志，不在当归也。”〉
value.en: He answered with a pun: ‘far ambition,’ not ‘return home.’
value.literal: Wei said: "A hundred qing of fine fields are not one acre—but one has yuanzhi medicine—not danggui.

value.zh: 後遷中監軍、征西將軍。
value.en: He rose to Central Inspector and General Who Campaigns West.
value.literal: Later promoted central army inspector and general who campaigns west.

value.zh: 趙氏之先，與秦共祖。
value.en: The Zhao clan's forebears shared an ancestor with Qin.
value.literal: Zhao clan's forebears, together with Qin shared ancestor.

value.zh: 至中衍，為帝大戊御。
value.en: Reaching Zhong Yan, he was Emperor Da Wu's charioteer.
value.literal: Reached Zhong Yan, was Emperor Da Wu's charioteer.

value.zh: 其後世蜚廉有子二人，而命其一子曰惡來，事紂，為周所殺，其後為秦。
value.en: In his later generations, Feilian had two sons, and named one of them Elai. Elai served King Zhou and was killed by the Zhou. His descendants became Qin.
value.literal: His later generations Feilian had sons two, and named his one son said Elai, served Zhou, was by Zhou killed, his descendants became Qin.

value.zh: 惡來弟曰季勝，其後為趙。
value.en: Elai's younger brother was named Jisheng. His descendants became Zhao.
value.literal: Elai's younger brother named Jisheng, his descendants became Zhao.

value.zh: 十八年，齊、魏伐我，我決河水灌之，兵去。
value.en: In the eighteenth year, Qi and Wei attacked Zhao. The Zhao forces breached the river dikes and flooded the invaders, forcing them to withdraw.
value.literal: Eighteenth year, Qi, Wei attacked us, we broke river water flooded them, troops left.

value.zh: 二十二年，張儀相秦。
value.en: In the twenty-second year, Zhang Yi became chancellor of Qin.
value.literal: Twenty-second year, Zhang Yi became prime minister of Qin.

value.zh: 趙疵與秦戰，敗，秦殺疵河西，取我藺、離石。
value.en: Zhao Ci fought against Qin and was defeated. Qin killed Ci west of the Yellow River and seized the Zhao cities of Lin and Lishi.
value.literal: Zhao Ci with Qin battled, defeated, Qin killed Ci river west, took our Lin, Li Shi.

value.zh: 二十三年，韓舉與齊、魏戰，死于桑丘。
value.en: In the twenty-third year, Han Ju fought against Qi and Wei and was killed at Sangqiu.
value.literal: Twenty-third year, Han Ju with Qi, Wei battled, died at Sang Qiu.

value.zh: 魏之先，畢公高之後也。
value.en: The forebears of the Wei clan were descendants of Duke Gao of Bi.
value.literal: The ancestors of Wei were descendants of Bi Gong Gao.

value.zh: 畢公高與周同姓。
value.en: Duke Gao of Bi shared the same surname as the royal house of Zhou.
value.literal: Bi Gong Gao shared the same surname with Zhou.

value.zh: 武王之伐紂，而高封於畢，於是為畢姓。
value.en: When King Wu conquered the tyrant Zhou, Gao was enfeoffed at Bi, and his descendants took Bi as their surname.
value.literal: When Wu Wang attacked Zhou, Gao was enfeoffed at Bi, thus becoming the Bi surname.

value.zh: 其後絕封，為庶人，或在中國，或在夷狄。
value.en: In later generations the line lost its fief, and its descendants became commoners, scattered across the Central States and among the barbarian lands.
value.literal: His descendants lost their enfeoffment and became commoners, some in the central states, some among the barbarians.

value.zh: 其苗裔曰畢萬，事晉獻公。
value.en: A distant descendant named Bi Wan entered the service of Duke Xian of Jin.
value.literal: His descendant was called Bi Wan and served Jin Xian Gong.

value.zh: 十二年，楚敗我襄陵。
value.en: In the twelfth year, Chu defeated our forces at Xiangling.
value.literal: In the twelfth year, Chu defeated our Xiang Ling.

value.zh: 諸侯執政與秦相張儀會齧桑。
value.en: The chief ministers of the feudal states met with Zhang Yi, the chancellor of Qin, at Niesang.
value.literal: The feudal lords' chief ministers met with Qin chancellor Zhang Yi at Nie Sang.

value.zh: 十三年，張儀相魏。
value.en: In the thirteenth year, Zhang Yi became the chancellor of Wei.
value.literal: In the thirteenth year, Zhang Yi became chancellor of Wei.

value.zh: 魏有女子化為丈夫。
value.en: In Wei, a woman transformed into a man.
value.literal: Wei had a woman who transformed into a man.

value.zh: 秦取我曲沃、平周。
value.en: Qin seized our cities of Quwo and Pingzhou.
value.literal: Qin took our Qu Wo and Ping Zhou.

value.zh: 十六年，襄王卒，子哀王立。
value.en: In the sixteenth year, King Xiang died. His son ascended the throne as King Ai.
value.literal: In the sixteenth year, Xiang Wang died. His son Ai Wang was established.

value.zh: 張儀復歸秦。
value.en: Zhang Yi returned once more to Qin.
value.literal: Zhang Yi again returned to Qin.

value.zh: 九年，與秦王會臨晉。
value.en: In the ninth year, Wei met with the King of Qin at Linjin.
value.literal: In the ninth year, they met with the Qin wang at Lin Jin.

value.zh: 張儀、魏章皆歸于魏。
value.en: Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang both returned to Wei.
value.literal: Zhang Yi and Wei Zhang all returned to Wei.

value.zh: 魏相田需死，楚害張儀、犀首、薛公。
value.en: The Wei chancellor Tian Xu died. Chu feared the influence of Zhang Yi, Xishou, and the Lord of Xue.
value.literal: The Wei chancellor Tian Xu died. Chu feared Zhang Yi, Xishou, and the Lord of Xue.

value.zh: 楚相昭魚謂蘇代曰：「田需死，吾恐張儀、犀首、薛公有一人相魏者也。」
value.en: The Chu chancellor Zhao Yu said to Su Dai, 'Now that Tian Xu is dead, I fear that one of those three — Zhang Yi, Xishou, or the Lord of Xue — will become chancellor of Wei.'
value.literal: Chu chancellor Zhao Yu told Su Dai said: 'Tian Xu died, I fear Zhang Yi, Xi Shou, Xue Gong have one chancellor Wei.'

value.zh: 代曰：「然相者欲誰而君便之？」
value.en: Su Dai replied, 'Then whom would you prefer as chancellor? Tell me, and I will make arrangements.'
value.literal: Dai said: 'So chancellor want who and lord convenient it?'

value.zh: 昭魚曰：「吾欲太子之自相也。」
value.en: Zhao Yu said, 'I would prefer the crown prince himself to serve as chancellor.'
value.literal: Zhao Yu said: 'I want crown prince self chancellor.'

value.zh: 代曰：「請為君北，必相之。」
value.en: Su Dai said, 'Allow me to go north on your behalf. I will see to it that he is made chancellor.'
value.literal: Dai said: 'Please for lord north, certainly chancellor it.'

value.zh: 昭魚曰：「柰何？」
value.en: Zhao Yu asked, 'How will you manage it?'
value.literal: Zhao Yu said: 'How?'

value.zh: 對曰：「君其為梁王，代請說君。」
value.en: Su Dai replied, 'Play the role of the King of Liang, and let me practice my argument on you.'
value.literal: Replied: 'Lord become Liang wang, Dai please persuade lord.'

value.zh: 昭魚曰：「柰何？」
value.en: Zhao Yu asked, 'How will you manage it?'
value.literal: Zhao Yu said: 'How?'

value.zh: 對曰：「代也從楚來，昭魚甚憂，曰：『田需死，吾恐張儀、犀首、薛公有一人相魏者也。』
value.en: Su Dai began, "I have just come from Chu. Zhao Yu is deeply worried. He said, 'Now that Tian Xu is dead, I fear that Zhang Yi, Xishou, or the Lord of Xue will become chancellor of Wei.'
value.literal: Replied: 'Dai from Chu come, Zhao Yu very worried, said: 'Tian Xu died, I fear Zhang Yi, Xi Shou, Xue Gong have one chancellor Wei.'

value.zh: 代曰：『梁王，長主也，必不相張儀。
value.en: I told him, 'The King of Liang is an experienced ruler. He will certainly not appoint Zhang Yi as chancellor.
value.literal: Dai said: 'Liang wang, senior lord, certainly not chancellor Zhang Yi.

value.zh: 張儀相，必右秦而左魏。
value.en: If Zhang Yi were made chancellor, he would surely favor Qin at Wei's expense.
value.literal: If Zhang Yi is chancellor, he will certainly favor Qin and slight Wei.

value.zh: 犀首相，必右韓而左魏。
value.en: If Xishou were made chancellor, he would favor Han at Wei's expense.
value.literal: If Xi Shou is chancellor, he will certainly favor Han and slight Wei.

value.zh: 薛公相，必右齊而左魏。
value.en: If the Lord of Xue were made chancellor, he would favor Qi at Wei's expense.
value.literal: If Xue Gong is chancellor, he will certainly favor Qi and slight Wei.

value.zh: 梁王，長主也，必不便也。』
value.en: The King of Liang is a seasoned ruler—he would surely find none of these acceptable.'
value.literal: Liang wang, senior lord, certainly not convenient.'

value.zh: 王曰：『然則寡人孰相？』
value.en: The King said, 'Then whom should I appoint as chancellor?'
value.literal: Wang said: 'So then I who chancellor?'

value.zh: 代曰：『莫若太子之自相。
value.en: Su Dai said, 'Nothing would be better than making the Crown Prince chancellor himself.
value.literal: Dai said: 'Nothing better than crown prince self chancellor.

value.zh: 太子之自相，是三人者皆以太子為非常相也，皆將務以其國事魏，欲得丞相璽也。
value.en: If the Crown Prince serves as chancellor, all three men will regard him as merely a temporary appointment. Each will then strive to devote his state's resources to serving Wei, hoping to obtain the chancellor's seal for himself.
value.literal: If the crown prince chancellors himself, these three will all consider the crown prince an extraordinary chancellor. They will all strive to have their states serve Wei in order to obtain the chancellor seal.

value.zh: 以魏之彊，而三萬乘之國輔之，魏必安矣。
value.en: With Wei's own strength, and three great powers of ten thousand chariots rallying behind it, Wei will surely be secure.
value.literal: With Wei's strength, and three ten-thousand-chariot states assisting it, Wei will certainly be peaceful.

value.zh: 故曰莫若太子之自相也。』」
value.en: That is why I say nothing would be better than the Crown Prince serving as chancellor himself.'"
value.literal: Therefore, said nothing better than crown prince self chancellor.'"

value.zh: 遂北見梁王，以此告之。
value.en: He then traveled north to see the King of Liang and presented this argument to him.
value.literal: He then went north and saw the Liang wang, telling him this.

value.zh: 太子果相魏。
value.en: The crown prince did in fact become chancellor of Wei.
value.literal: The crown prince indeed became chancellor of Wei.

value.zh: 十年，張儀死。
value.en: In the tenth year, Zhang Yi died.
value.literal: In the tenth year, Zhang Yi died.

value.zh: 十一年，與秦武王會應。
value.en: In the eleventh year, the King met with King Wu of Qin at Ying.
value.literal: In the eleventh year, they met with Qin Wu Wang at Ying.

value.zh: 十二年，太子朝於秦。
value.en: In the twelfth year, the Crown Prince traveled to Qin for an audience.
value.literal: In the twelfth year, the crown prince went for audience in Qin.

value.zh: 秦來伐我皮氏，未拔而解。
value.en: Qin attacked our city of Pishi but failed to take it and withdrew.
value.literal: Qin came and attacked our Pi Shi, but did not capture it and retreated.

value.zh: 十四年，秦來歸武王后。
value.en: In the fourteenth year, Qin sent back the queen of King Wu.
value.literal: In the fourteenth year, Qin came and returned the Wu Wang queen.

value.zh: 十六年，秦拔我蒲反、陽晉、封陵。
value.en: In the sixteenth year, Qin captured our cities of Pufan, Yangjin, and Fengling.
value.literal: In the sixteenth year, Qin captured our Pu Fan, Yang Jin, and Feng Ling.

value.zh: 十七年，與秦會臨晉。
value.en: In the seventeenth year, the King met with Qin at Linjin.
value.literal: In the seventeenth year, they met with Qin at Lin Jin.

value.zh: 秦予我蒲反。
value.en: Qin returned Pufan to us.
value.literal: Qin gave us Pu Fan.

value.zh: 十八年，與秦伐楚。
value.en: In the eighteenth year, Wei joined Qin in attacking Chu.
value.literal: In the eighteenth year, they attacked Chu with Qin.

value.zh: 二十一年，與齊、韓共敗秦軍函谷。
value.en: In the twenty-first year, Wei joined with Qi and Han to defeat the Qin army at Hangu Pass.
value.literal: In the twenty-first year, with Qi and Han they together defeated the Qin army at Han Gu.

value.zh: 陳完者，陳厲公他之子也。
value.en: Chen Wan was the son of Duke Li of Chen, whose personal name was Ta.
value.literal: Chen Wan was the son of Chen Li Gong Ta.

value.zh: 完生，周太史過陳，陳厲公使卜完，卦得觀之否：「是為觀國之光，利用賓于王。
value.en: When Wan was born, the Grand Astrologer of Zhou happened to pass through the state of Chen. Duke Li had him cast a divination for the child. The hexagram obtained was Guan changing to Pi, and the reading declared: 'This signifies one who shall observe the glory of a state, and it is auspicious for him to serve as a guest of a king.
value.literal: When Wan was born, the Grand Astrologer of Zhou passed through Chen. Duke Li of Chen had him divine for Wan. The hexagram obtained was Guan changing to Pi: 'This means observing the glory of the state, advantageous to be a guest of the king.

value.zh: 此其代陳有國乎？
value.en: Could it be that his line will one day supplant Chen and possess a state of its own?
value.literal: Will this one replace Chen and possess a state?

value.zh: 不在此而在異國乎？
value.en: Yet perhaps not in this state, but in a foreign land?
value.literal: Not in this state but in a different state?

value.zh: 非此其身也，在其子孫。
value.en: It will not come to pass in his own lifetime, but through his descendants.
value.literal: Not in this person himself, but in his descendants.

value.zh: 若在異國，必姜姓。
value.en: If it is to be in a foreign state, then it must be one ruled by the Jiang clan.
value.literal: If in a different state, it must be a state of the Jiang surname.

value.zh: 姜姓，四嶽之後。
value.en: The Jiang are descendants of the Four Peaks.
value.literal: The Jiang surname are descendants of the Four Peaks.

value.zh: 物莫能兩大，陳衰，此其昌乎？」
value.en: Nothing in this world can sustain two great powers at once — when Chen declines, his line shall surely flourish."
value.literal: No thing can have two greats; when Chen declines, this one shall flourish.'

value.zh: 十九年，宣王卒，子湣王地立。
value.en: In the nineteenth year, King Xuan died. His son, King Min, whose personal name was Di, succeeded him.
value.literal: In the nineteenth year, King Xuan died. His son King Min Di succeeded him.

value.zh: 湣王元年，秦使張儀與諸侯執政會於齧桑。
value.en: In the first year of King Min, Qin sent Zhang Yi to meet the chief ministers of the feudal lords at Niesang.
value.literal: In King Min's first year, Qin sent Zhang Yi to meet with the governing ministers of the feudal lords at Niesang.

value.zh: 三年，封田嬰於薛。
value.en: In the third year, Tian Ying received Xue as his fief.
value.literal: In the third year, Tian Ying was enfeoffed at Xue.

value.zh: 四年，迎婦於秦。
value.en: In the fourth year, he brought in a bride from Qin.
value.literal: In the fourth year, he welcomed a bride from Qin.

value.zh: 七年，與宋攻魏，敗之觀澤。
value.en: In the seventh year, Qi joined Song in attacking Wei and defeated it at Guanze.
value.literal: In the seventh year, he joined Song in attacking Wei and defeated it at Guanze.

value.zh: 十二年，攻魏。
value.en: In the twelfth year of King Min's reign, Qi attacked Wei.
value.literal: In the twelfth year, they attacked Wei.

value.zh: 楚圍雍氏，秦敗屈丐。
value.en: At the same time, Chu besieged the city of Yongshi, and Qin defeated the Chu general Qu Gai.
value.literal: Chu besieged Yongshi. Qin defeated Qu Gai.

value.zh: 蘇代謂田軫曰：「臣願有謁於公，其為事甚完，使楚利公，成為福，不成亦為福。
value.en: Su Dai addressed Tian Zhen: "I have a proposal for you, my lord. The plan is airtight: whether it succeeds or fails, it will work to your advantage in relation to Chu.
value.literal: Su Dai said to Tian Zhen: 'Your servant wishes to present something to you. The plan is very thorough: if Chu benefits you, success is fortunate, and failure is also fortunate.

value.zh: 今者臣立於門，客有言曰魏王謂韓馮、張儀曰：『煮棗將拔，齊兵又進，子來救寡人則可矣；
value.en: Today, as I stood at the gate, a visitor reported that the King of Wei told Han Feng and Zhang Yi: 'Zaozao is about to fall, and the army of Qi presses forward. Come to my rescue, and all will be well.
value.literal: Today as I stood at the gate, a guest said that the King of Wei told Han Feng and Zhang Yi: 'Zaozao is about to fall, and Qi's army advances further. If you come to rescue me, it will be sufficient.

value.zh: 不救寡人，寡人弗能拔。』
value.en: If you do not rescue me, I shall not be able to hold out.'
value.literal: If you do not rescue me, I will not be able to hold out.'

value.zh: 此特轉辭也。
value.en: But this is merely a diplomatic ploy.
value.literal: This is merely a diversionary statement.

value.zh: 秦、韓之兵毋東，旬餘，則魏氏轉韓從秦，秦逐張儀，交臂而事齊楚，此公之事成也。」
value.en: If the troops of Qin and Han do not march east, then within ten days Wei will detach Han from Qin's cause, Qin will dismiss Zhang Yi, and they will all clasp hands to serve Qi and Chu. Then your designs will be realized."
value.literal: If the troops of Qin and Han do not move east, then within ten days Wei will shift Han to follow Qin, Qin will send Zhang Yi away, and they will join together to serve Qi and Chu — then your affairs will be accomplished.'

value.zh: 田軫曰：「柰何使無東？」
value.en: Tian Zhen asked: "But how can we prevent them from marching east?"
value.literal: Tian Zhen asked: 'How can we prevent them from marching east?'

value.zh: 對曰：「韓馮之救魏之辭，必不謂韓王曰『馮以為魏』，必曰『馮將以秦韓之兵東卻齊宋，馮因摶三國之兵，乘屈丐之獘，南割於楚，故地必盡得之矣』。
value.en: Su Dai replied: "When Han Feng makes his case for rescuing Wei, he will never tell the King of Han, 'I am doing this for Wei.' Instead, he will say: 'I shall lead the combined forces of Qin and Han eastward to repel Qi and Song. Then I shall unite the armies of three states, exploit Qu Gai's defeat, and carve territory from Chu in the south. All the old lands shall surely be recovered.'
value.literal: He replied: 'When Han Feng argues for rescuing Wei, he will certainly not tell the King of Han "Feng does this for Wei's sake." He will surely say: "Feng will use the troops of Qin and Han to drive Qi and Song eastward, then unite the three states' armies, exploit Qu Gai's defeat, and carve territory from Chu to the south — all the former lands will be recovered.'

value.zh: 張儀救魏之辭，必不謂秦王曰『儀以為魏』，必曰『儀且以秦韓之兵東距齊宋，儀將摶三國之兵，乘屈丐之獘，南割於楚，名存亡國，實伐三川而歸，此王業也』。
value.en: Likewise, when Zhang Yi argues for rescuing Wei, he will never tell the King of Qin, 'I am doing this for Wei.' He will say: 'I shall lead the forces of Qin and Han eastward to block Qi and Song, then unite the three states' armies, exploit Qu Gai's defeat, and seize territory from Chu. In name, we save a perishing state; in reality, we conquer Sanchuan and return in triumph. This is the enterprise of a true king.'
value.literal: Zhang Yi's argument for rescuing Wei will certainly not tell the King of Qin 'Yi does this for Wei.' He will surely say: 'Yi will lead the troops of Qin and Han east to repel Qi and Song, then unite the three states' armies, exploit Qu Gai's defeat, carve territory from Chu in the south — in name saving a perishing state, in reality attacking Sanchuan and returning. This is a royal enterprise.'

value.zh: 公令楚王與韓氏地，使秦制和，謂秦王曰『請與韓地，而王以施三川，韓氏之兵不用而得地於楚』。
value.en: If you persuade the King of Chu to cede land to Han and let Qin broker the peace, saying to the King of Qin: 'Grant land to Han, and Your Majesty may extend your influence over Sanchuan. Han's armies need not march, and yet they gain territory from Chu.'
value.literal: If you have the King of Chu give land to Han and let Qin mediate the peace, saying to the King of Qin: 'Please give land to Han, and the King can bestow his favor upon Sanchuan. Han's troops need not be used and they will gain territory from Chu.'

value.zh: 韓馮之東兵之辭且謂秦何？
value.en: And what will Han Feng say to Qin when he argues for sending troops east?
value.literal: What will Han Feng say to Qin in his argument for marching the troops east?

value.zh: 曰『秦兵不用而得三川，伐楚韓以窘魏，魏氏不敢東，是孤齊也』。
value.en: He will say: 'Qin gains Sanchuan without deploying a single soldier, while attacking Chu and Han corners Wei. Wei will not dare move east — and Qi will be isolated.'
value.literal: He will say: 'Qin gains Sanchuan without using its troops, attacks Chu and Han to corner Wei, Wei dares not move east — this isolates Qi.'

value.zh: 張儀之東兵之辭且謂何？
value.en: And what will Zhang Yi say in his argument for sending troops east?
value.literal: What will Zhang Yi say in his argument for marching troops east?

value.zh: 曰『秦韓欲地而兵有案，聲威發於魏，魏氏之欲不失齊楚者有資矣』。
value.en: He will say: 'Qin and Han desire territory while keeping their armies in reserve. Their military prestige is directed at Wei, and Wei's desire to maintain ties with Qi and Chu will have the leverage it needs.'
value.literal: He will say: 'Qin and Han desire territory while their troops stand ready. The prestige and power are directed at Wei; Wei's desire not to lose Qi and Chu will have resources to rely on.'

value.zh: 魏氏轉秦韓爭事齊楚，楚王欲而無與地，公令秦韓之兵不用而得地，有一大德也。
value.en: Wei will then redirect Qin and Han into competing to serve Qi and Chu. The King of Chu desires this outcome but has offered no territory. If you enable Qin and Han to acquire territory without deploying their armies, that will be an immense favor.
value.literal: Wei will then shift Qin and Han into competing to serve Qi and Chu. The King of Chu wishes this but has given no territory. You enable Qin and Han to gain territory without using their troops — this is one great favor.

value.zh: 秦韓之王劫於韓馮、張儀而東兵以徇服魏，公常執左券以責於秦韓，此其善於公而惡張子多資矣。」
value.en: If the kings of Qin and Han are pressured by Han Feng and Zhang Yi to march east and coerce Wei, you will always hold the tally against Qin and Han. This arrangement greatly favors you while undermining Zhang Yi."
value.literal: If the kings of Qin and Han are pressured by Han Feng and Zhang Yi to march east and coerce Wei into submission, you will always hold the left half of the tally to make demands upon Qin and Han. This benefits you greatly while working against Zhang Yi.'

value.zh: 賈易，字明叔，無為人。
value.en: Jia Yi, courtesy name Mingshu, came from Wuwei.
value.literal: Jia Yi, styled Mingshu, was a native of Wuwei.

value.zh: 七歲而孤。
value.en: He lost his father when he was seven.
value.literal: At seven he was orphaned.

value.zh: 母彭，以紡績自給，日與易十錢，使從學。
value.en: His mother Peng earned their living by spinning and weaving, giving Yi ten copper cash a day for his schooling.
value.literal: His mother Peng supported herself by spinning and weaving, giving Yi ten cash each day so he could study.

value.zh: 易不忍使一錢，每浹旬，輒復歸之。
value.en: Yi hated to spend even one coin; every ten days or so he would bring the money back to her.
value.literal: Yi could not bear to spend a single cash; every ten days he would return them.

value.zh: 年逾冠，中進士甲科，調常州司法參軍。
value.en: After he came of age, he placed in the top tier of the jinshi examination and was appointed judicial adjutant in Changzhou.
value.literal: After coming of age he passed the jinshi in the top class and was appointed judicial adjutant in Changzhou.

value.zh: 自以儒者不閑法令，歲議獄，唯求合於人情，曰：「人情所在，法亦在焉。」
value.en: He regarded himself as a scholar of the classics, not versed in penal law; when he heard cases each year he looked only for what matched common human feeling, saying, "Where human feeling is, the law is as well."
value.literal: Considering himself a Confucian scholar unfamiliar with statutes, when he reviewed cases each year he sought only what accorded with human feeling, saying: "Where human feeling lies, the law lies there too."

value.zh: 訖去，郡中稱平。
value.en: By the time he left office, the prefecture praised his judgments as even-handed.
value.literal: When he left at the end of his term, the prefecture called his judgments fair.

value.zh: 論曰：賈易初以剛直名，觀其再劾文彥博、范純仁，而斥蘇軾、蘇轍尤甚，何以剛直為哉？
value.en: Commentary: Jia Yi was first known for blunt integrity—yet when one sees him twice impeach Wen Yanbo and Fan Chunren, and attack Su Shi and Su Zhe with special venom, how can he be called upright?
value.literal: Commentary: Jia Yi was first known for blunt uprightness—yet seeing him twice impeach Wen Yanbo and Fan Chunren, and especially reproach Su Shi and Su Zhe, how can this be called uprightness?

value.zh: 董敦逸於元祐末與黃慶基誣二蘇，以開紹聖之禍，及紹聖則肆詆元祐諸臣，甚至瑤華之冤不能持正，雖終悔而諫，亦何及焉。
value.en: At the end of Yuanyou, Dong Dunyi and Huang Qingji falsely accused the two Su brothers, opening the calamity of Shaosheng; when Shaosheng arrived he wantonly reviled the Yuanyou ministers, and even in the injustice done to Princess Yaohua could not stand for what was right; though he finally repented and remonstrated, what good did that do?
value.literal: Dong Dunyi at the end of Yuanyou together with Huang Qingji falsely accused the two Su brothers, opening the calamity of Shaosheng; when Shaosheng came he wantonly vilified Yuanyou ministers, and even in the injustice of Yaohua could not hold to what was right; though he finally repented and remonstrated, what good was it?

value.zh: 及見蔡京、蔡卞稔惡，乃論其過惡以自文，杯水不足以救車薪之火也。
value.en: Only when he saw Cai Jing and Cai Bian's accumulated evil did he denounce their crimes to clear himself—a cup of water cannot quench a cartload of burning kindling.
value.literal: Only when he saw Cai Jing and Cai Bian's accumulated wickedness did he discuss their faults to exculpate himself—a cup of water cannot save a cartload of burning firewood.

value.zh: 上官均諫切中時事，及不從紹述之議，其為人若可觀，然論呂大防、蘇轍，以之再黜，是亦助紹述者也。
value.en: Shang Guanjun's remonstrances cut to the heart of current affairs, and in refusing the "continuation" agenda he seemed a man of substance; yet in securing a second demotion for Lü Dafang and Su Zhe, he too served the "continuation" cause.
value.literal: Shang Guanjun's remonstrances keenly hit the affairs of the time, and in not following the "continuation" program his conduct seemed admirable; yet in getting Lü Dafang and Su Zhe demoted a second time, he too aided the "continuation."

value.zh: 楊畏傾危反覆，周流不窮，雖儀、秦縱橫，無以尚之，豈徒有三變而已。
value.en: Yang Wei's treacherous reversals flowed on without end—even the coalition masters Yi and Qin could not surpass him; was it merely three changes?
value.literal: Yang Wei's subversive reversals flowed on without end—even Yi and Qin in coalition tactics could not surpass him; was it only three changes?

value.zh: 至於倡紹述以取信哲宗，又謂王安石之學有聖人意，可謂小人無忌憚也哉。
value.en: To promote "continuation" in order to win Zhezong's trust, and to declare that Wang Anshi's learning captured the sage's intent—such a man may truly be called utterly shameless.
value.literal: As for advocating "continuation" to win Zhezong's trust, and also saying Wang Anshi's learning had the sage's intent, one could call this a petty man utterly without scruple.

value.zh: 來之邵盡擊時賢而進章惇、安燾、呂惠卿，又請加美諡於安石，其流惡不已，乃誣人非其子而欲掩其貲，亦何所不至焉。
value.en: Lai Zhi Shao attacked every worthy man of the age while pushing Zhang Dun, An Tao, and Lü Huiqing forward, and even sought a posthumous honorific for Anshi; his stream of wickedness never ceased—he would falsely deny a man's paternity to seize his property; what would he stop at?
value.literal: Lai Zhi Shao attacked all worthy men of the time while advancing Zhang Dun, An Tao, and Lü Huiqing, and also asked to add a posthumous honorific to Anshi; his stream of wickedness did not cease—he even falsely claimed a man was not his father's son to seize his property; what would he not do?

value.zh: 葉濤在太學，已著汙跡，擢第之後，諂安石而從之學，後得曾布之薦，凡元祐名賢貶責制辭，肆筆醜詆，雖有善猶不能自滌，況無可述者乎！
value.en: Ye Tao had already stained his name at the Imperial University; after passing the examination he flattered Anshi and followed his learning; later, through Zeng Bu's patronage, he drafted every edict demoting a Yuanyou worthy in language of vile abuse—even had he possessed virtue he could not have cleansed himself, much less when there was nothing worth recounting!
value.literal: Ye Tao at the Imperial University already left filthy traces; after passing the examination he flattered Anshi and followed his learning; later through Zeng Bu's recommendation, for every demotion edict of a Yuanyou worthy he wielded the brush in vile abuse—even if he had virtue he still could not cleanse himself, much less when there was nothing to recount!

value.zh: 〇陳靖張綸邵曄崔立魯有開張逸吳遵路趙尚寬高賦程師孟韓晉卿葉康直
value.en: Chen Jing, Zhang Lun, Shao Ye, Cui Li, Lu Youkai, Zhang Yi, Wu Zunlu, Zhao Shangkuan, Gao Fu, Cheng Shimeng, Han Jinqing, and Ye Kangzhi.
value.literal: Chen Jing, Zhang Lun, Shao Ye, Cui Li, Lu Youkai, Zhang Yi, Wu Zunlu, Zhao Shangkuan, Gao Fu, Cheng Shimeng, Han Jinqing, Ye Kangzhi.

value.zh: 儒林四
value.en: Confucian Scholars 4
value.literal: Confucian Scholars 4.

value.zh: 改知嚴道縣，攝通判嘉定。
value.en: He was reassigned to govern Yandao County and served as acting vice prefect of Jiading.
value.literal: He was changed to govern Yandao County and acted as Vice Prefect of Jiading.

value.zh: 白厓砦將王塤引蠻寇利店，刑獄使者置塤於法，又罥絓餘人當坐死。
value.en: Baiya Fort commander Wang Kun led barbarian raiders against Lidian; the judicial envoy executed Kun and implicated others for death.
value.literal: The Baiya Fort commander Wang Kun led barbarian raiders against Lidian; the judicial envoy punished Kun by law and also implicated others who should die.

value.zh: 泰之訪知夷都實邇利店，夷都蠻稱亂，不需引導，固請釋之，不聽。
value.en: Taizhi found the Yidu tribe lay next to Lidian and had been called rebels without needing a guide—he pleaded for their release in vain.
value.literal: Taizhi investigated and learned that the Yidu tribe actually bordered Lidian; the Yidu barbarians were called rebels and needed no guide—he firmly requested release but was not heeded.

value.zh: 乃去官。
value.en: He resigned.
value.literal: He thereupon left office.

value.zh: 宣撫使安丙薦之曰：“蜀中名儒楊虞仲之子，當逆臣之變，勉有位者毋動。
value.en: Pacification Commissioner An Bing recommended him: "Taizhi, son of the famed Shu scholar Yang Yuzhong, urged officials to hold firm when the rebel crisis came.
value.literal: Pacification Commissioner An Bing recommended him, saying: "Taizhi, son of the famous Shu scholar Yang Yuzhong—when the rebellious minister's crisis came, he urged those in office not to stir.

value.zh: 言不用，拂衣而去。
value.en: When ignored he shook out his robes and left.
value.literal: When his words were not used he shook out his robes and left.

value.zh: 使得尺寸之柄，必能見危致命。”
value.en: Given even a little authority he would meet danger and give his life."
value.literal: If granted even a small measure of authority he would surely be able to meet peril and give his life."

value.zh: 召泰之赴都堂審察，以親老辭。
value.en: Taizhi was summoned to the Secretariat for review but declined, citing aged parents.
value.literal: Taizhi was summoned to the Secretariat for examination; citing aged parents he declined.

value.zh: 差知廣安軍，未上，丁父憂。
value.en: He was assigned Guang'an Army but entered mourning for his father before taking up the post.
value.literal: He was assigned to govern Guang'an Army; before he took up the post he entered mourning for his father.

value.zh: 免喪，知富順監。
value.en: After mourning he governed the Fushun salt monopoly.
value.literal: When mourning ended he governed Fushun Salt Monopoly.

value.zh: 去官，以祿稟數千緡予鄰裏，以千緡為義莊。
value.en: On leaving office he gave thousands of strings of salary to neighbors and a thousand to a charity estate.
value.literal: Leaving office he gave several thousand strings of his salary to neighbors and a thousand strings to a charity estate.

value.zh: 知普州，以安居、安嶽二縣受禍尤慘，泰之力白丙盡蠲其賦。
value.en: As prefect of Puzhou he persuaded An Bing to remit levies entirely for Anju and Anyue, which had suffered worst.
value.literal: Governing Puzhou, because Anju and Anyue two counties had suffered especially cruel harm, Taizhi strongly told Bing to remit their levies entirely.

value.zh: 丙復薦於朝，召赴行在，固辭。
value.en: An Bing recommended him again; summoned to court he firmly declined.
value.literal: Bing again recommended him to the court and he was summoned to the traveling palace; he firmly declined.

value.zh: 知果州。
value.en: He was appointed to govern Guozhou.
value.literal: He was appointed to govern Guozhou.

value.zh: 踦零錢病民，泰之以一年經費儲其贏為諸邑對減，上尚書省，按為定式。
value.en: The qiling coin levy hurt the people; Taizhi saved a year's surplus to cut levies across prefectures, reported upward, and it became fixed practice.
value.literal: The qiling coin levy harmed the people; Taizhi stored one year's surplus from routine expenses to reduce levies across prefectures in pairs, reported to the Ministry of Revenue, and it was adopted as a fixed pattern.

value.zh: 民歌之曰：“前張後楊，惠我無疆。”
value.en: The people sang: "First Zhang, then Yang—bless us without end."
value.literal: The people sang: "First Zhang then Yang—bless us without end."

value.zh: 張謂張義，實自發其端，而泰之踵行之。
value.en: Zhang was Zhang Yi, who began the practice; Taizhi followed.
value.literal: Zhang meant Zhang Yi—he actually began it, and Taizhi followed in his steps.

value.zh: 任城王雲，年五歲，恭宗崩，號哭不絕聲。
value.en: Yun, Prince of Rencheng, was only five when Gongzong died, yet he wailed without stopping.
value.literal: Yun, Prince of Rencheng, was five years old when Gongzong died, and he wailed without cease.

value.zh: 世祖聞之而呼，抱之泣曰：「汝何知而有成人之意也！」
value.en: Shizu heard and called for him, took him in his arms, and wept. "How is it that you already have a grown man's heart?"
value.literal: Shizu heard of this, summoned him, embraced him, and wept, saying, "What do you know, to have the mind of a grown man?"

value.zh: 和平五年封，拜使持節、侍中、征東大將軍、和龍鎮都大將。
value.en: In Heping year 5 he received his fief and was made Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and commander of Helong Garrison.
value.literal: In Heping year 5 he was enfeoffed and appointed Bearer of the Staff, Palace Attendant, Grand General Who Conquers the East, and grand commander of Helong Garrison.

value.zh: 顯祖時，拜都督中外諸軍事、中都坐大官，聽理民訟，甚收時譽。
value.en: Under Xianzu he commanded the armies inside and outside the court, served as seated high minister of the central capital, heard civil suits, and won wide renown.
value.literal: Under Xianzu he was appointed commander of all military affairs within and beyond the court and seated high minister of the central capital; he heard civil lawsuits and won great praise in his time.

value.zh: 延興中，顯祖集羣僚，欲禪位於京兆王子推。
value.en: During the Yanxing era, Xianzu gathered his ministers, intending to abdicate to Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao.
value.literal: During Yanxing, Xianzu assembled the officials and wished to abdicate to Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao.

value.zh: 王公卿士，莫敢先言。
value.en: Among the princes, dukes, ministers, and officers, no one dared speak first.
value.literal: None among the princes, dukes, ministers, and officers dared speak first.

value.zh: 雲進曰：「陛下方隆太平，臨覆四海，豈得上違宗廟，下棄兆民。
value.en: Yun stepped forward. "Your Majesty is raising an age of peace and shelters all within the four seas. How could you turn away from the ancestral temples above and cast off the people below?
value.literal: Yun stepped forward and said, "Your Majesty is now exalting great peace and overseeing all within the four seas; how could you above violate the ancestral temples and below abandon the myriad people?

value.zh: 父子相傳，其來久矣，皇魏之興，未之有革。
value.en: Father-to-son succession has long been the rule; since imperial Wei arose, it has never been altered.
value.literal: The succession from father to son has come down for a long time; since the rise of imperial Wei, it has not been changed.

value.zh: 皇儲正統，聖德夙章。
value.en: The crown prince is the rightful heir, and his virtue has shone since early youth.
value.literal: The crown prince is the orthodox heir, and his sagely virtue was manifest early.

value.zh: 陛下必欲割捐塵務，頤神清曠者，冢副之寄，宜紹寶曆，若欲捨儲，輕移宸極，恐非先聖之意，駭動人情。
value.en: If Your Majesty truly wishes to lay aside worldly affairs and nourish your spirit in quiet freedom, the throne should pass to the heir. If you set the heir aside and lightly move the imperial pivot, I fear this defies the former sages and will shock the hearts of men.
value.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to cut away worldly affairs and nourish the spirit in clear freedom, the charge of the heir should continue the precious calendar; if you mean to set aside the heir and lightly shift the imperial pivot, I fear it is not the intention of the former sages and will alarm human feeling.

value.zh: 又，天下是祖宗之天下，而陛下輒改神器，上乖七廟七靈，下長姦亂之道，此是禍福所由，願深思慎之。」
value.en: Moreover, the realm belongs to the ancestors. If Your Majesty suddenly changes the sacred vessel, you will offend the ancestral spirits above and open the way to treachery and disorder below. Fortune and disaster begin here; please think deeply and proceed with care."
value.literal: Moreover, the realm belongs to the ancestors, yet Your Majesty would suddenly change the sacred vessel, above going against the seven temples and seven spirits and below lengthening the road of treachery and disorder. This is where fortune and disaster begin; I beg you to think deeply and act carefully."

value.zh: 太尉源賀又進曰：「陛下今欲外選諸王而禪位于皇叔者，臣恐春秋蒸嘗，昭穆有亂，脫萬世之後，必有逆饗之譏，深願思任城之言。」
value.en: Grand Marshal Yuan He also spoke. "If Your Majesty chooses from among the princes and abdicates to an imperial uncle, I fear the order of the ancestral rites will be thrown into confusion, and later ages will condemn the offerings as improper. I beg you to weigh Rencheng's words."
value.literal: Grand Marshal Yuan He also stepped forward and said, "If Your Majesty now wishes to choose externally among the princes and abdicate to an imperial uncle, I fear that in spring and autumn sacrifices the order of Zhao and Mu will be confused, and after ten thousand generations there will surely be criticism of improper offerings. I earnestly hope you will consider Rencheng's words."

value.zh: 東陽公元丕等進曰：「皇太子雖聖德夙彰，然實沖幼。
value.en: Duke Yuan Pi of Dongyang and the others added, "Although the crown prince's virtue is already clear, he is still very young.
value.literal: Duke Yuan Pi of Dongyang and the others advanced and said, "Though the crown prince's sagely virtue has long been evident, he is in truth still young.

value.zh: 陛下富於春秋，始覽機政，普天景仰，率土傒心，欲隆獨善，不以萬物為意，其若宗廟何，其若億兆何！」
value.en: Your Majesty is young and has only begun to govern; all under heaven look to you, and every land waits on your heart. If you prize private purity and give no thought to the world, what becomes of the ancestral temples? What becomes of the people?"
value.literal: Your Majesty is rich in years and has only begun to oversee the mechanisms of government; all under heaven look up to you, and the whole land waits with longing. If you wish to exalt solitary goodness and give no thought to the myriad things, what of the ancestral temples? What of the millions of people?"

value.zh: 顯祖曰：「儲宮正統，受終文祖，羣公相之，有何不可。」
value.en: Xianzu replied, "The crown prince is the rightful line, receiving the succession from Wenzu. With all of you to assist him, what could be wrong?"
value.literal: Xianzu said, "The heir's palace is the orthodox line; he received the completion from Wenzu. If all you gentlemen assist him, what is unacceptable?"

value.zh: 於是傳位於高祖。
value.en: Thereupon he passed the throne to Gaozu.
value.literal: Thereupon he passed the throne to Gaozu.

value.zh: 後蠕蠕犯塞，雲為中軍大都督，從顯祖討之，遇於大磧。
value.en: Later, when the Rouran raided the frontier, Yun served as grand commander of the central army and followed Xianzu against them, meeting them in the great desert.
value.literal: Later, when the Rouran violated the frontier, Yun became grand commander of the central army, followed Xianzu in campaigning against them, and met them in the great desert.

value.zh: 事具蠕蠕傳。
value.en: The affair is recorded in the Rouran biography.
value.literal: The matter is fully recorded in the Rouran biography.

value.zh: 後仇池氐反，以雲為征西大將軍討平之。
value.en: Later, when the Qiuchi Di rebelled, Yun was made Grand General Who Conquers the West and put them down.
value.literal: Later, when the Di of Qiuchi rebelled, Yun was made Grand General Who Conquers the West and suppressed them.

value.zh: 除都督徐兗二州緣淮諸軍事、征東大將軍、開府、徐州刺史。
value.en: He was appointed commander of military affairs along the Huai in Xu and Yan provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, opened his office, and served as inspector of Xu Province.
value.literal: He was appointed commander of military affairs along the Huai in Xu and Yan provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the East, with an opened office, and Inspector of Xu Province.

value.zh: 雲以太妃蓋氏薨，表求解任，顯祖不許，雲悲號動疾，乃許之。
value.en: When Yun's grand consort, Lady Gai, died, he asked to resign. Xianzu refused, but Yun grieved and wailed until he fell ill, and only then was he allowed to step down.
value.literal: When Yun's grand consort, Lady Gai, died, he memorialized requesting release from office. Xianzu refused; Yun's grief and wailing brought on illness, and only then was he permitted.

value.zh: 性善撫綏，得徐方之心，為百姓所追戀。
value.en: He was naturally good at soothing and governing people, won the hearts of Xu, and was remembered fondly by its people.
value.literal: By nature he was good at comforting and pacifying people, won the hearts of the Xu region, and was long remembered by the commoners.

value.zh: 送遺錢貨，一無所受。
value.en: He refused every gift of money or goods sent to him.
value.literal: Of the money and goods sent to him as gifts, he accepted not a single thing.

value.zh: 顯祖聞而嘉之。
value.en: Xianzu heard of this and praised him.
value.literal: Xianzu heard of this and praised him.

value.zh: 復拜侍中、中都大官，賜帛千匹、羊千口。
value.en: He was again made Palace Attendant and high minister of the central capital, and received a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand sheep.
value.literal: He was again appointed Palace Attendant and high minister of the central capital, and was granted a thousand bolts of silk and a thousand sheep.

value.zh: 出為冀州刺史，仍本將軍。
value.en: He was sent out as inspector of Ji Province, retaining his former general's rank.
value.literal: He went out as Inspector of Ji Province, retaining his original generalship.

value.zh: 雲留心政事，甚得下情，於是合州請戶輸絹五尺、粟五升以報雲恩。
value.en: Yun governed attentively and understood those under him so well that the whole province asked to give five chi of silk and five sheng of grain per household in gratitude for his kindness.
value.literal: Yun gave close attention to government and greatly won the feelings of those below; thereupon the whole province requested that each household contribute five chi of silk and five sheng of grain to repay Yun's kindness.

value.zh: 高祖嘉之，遷使持節、都督陝西諸軍事、征南大將軍、長安鎮都大將、雍州刺史。
value.en: Gaozu praised him and transferred him to serve as Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Shaanxi, Grand General Who Conquers the South, commander of Chang'an Garrison, and inspector of Yong Province.
value.literal: Gaozu praised him and transferred him as Bearer of the Staff, commander of military affairs in Shaanxi, Grand General Who Conquers the South, grand commander of Chang'an Garrison, and Inspector of Yong Province.

value.zh: 雲廉謹自修，留心庶獄，挫抑豪強，羣盜息止，州民頌之者千有餘人。
value.en: Yun was upright and careful, gave close attention to common lawsuits, checked the powerful, and brought banditry to an end; more than a thousand people in the province praised him in verse.
value.literal: Yun cultivated himself in integrity and caution, attended carefully to ordinary lawsuits, suppressed the powerful and arrogant, and bandits ceased; more than a thousand people of the province sang his praises.

value.zh: 文明太后嘉之，賜帛千匹。
value.en: Empress Dowager Wenming praised him and gave him a thousand bolts of silk.
value.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming praised him and granted him a thousand bolts of silk.

value.zh: 太和五年，薨於州。
value.en: In Taihe year 5 he died in office in the province.
value.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, he died in the province.

value.zh: 遺令薄葬，勿受賵禭。
value.en: In his last instructions he ordered a simple burial and forbade the acceptance of funerary gifts.
value.literal: His final instructions ordered a modest burial and forbade acceptance of funerary gifts.

value.zh: 諸子奉遵其旨。
value.en: His sons carried out his wishes.
value.literal: His sons respectfully followed his wishes.

value.zh: 喪至京師，車駕親臨，哭之哀慟，贈以本官，諡曰康。
value.en: When his coffin reached the capital, the emperor came in person and wept bitterly over him; Yun was posthumously restored to his offices and titled Kang.
value.literal: When the coffin reached the capital, the emperor came in person, wept over him with deep grief, posthumously granted him his former offices, and gave him the title Kang.

value.zh: 陪葬雲中之金陵。
value.en: He was buried alongside the Jinling mausoleum at Yunzhong.
value.literal: He was buried beside the Jinling at Yunzhong.

value.zh: 雲長子澄，字道鎮，少而好學。
value.en: Yun's eldest son Cheng, styled Daozhen, loved learning from an early age.
value.literal: Yun's eldest son Cheng, courtesy name Daozhen, loved learning from youth.

value.zh: 及康王薨，澄居喪以孝聞。
value.en: After Prince Kang died, Cheng became known for filial devotion in mourning.
value.literal: When Prince Kang died, Cheng became known for filial conduct during mourning.

value.zh: 襲封，加征北大將軍。
value.en: He inherited the fief and was given the added rank Grand General Who Conquers the North.
value.literal: He inherited the fief and was additionally made Grand General Who Conquers the North.

value.zh: 高祖時，蠕蠕犯塞，加澄使持節、都督北討諸軍事以討之。
value.en: Under Gaozu, when the Rouran raided the frontier, Cheng was made Bearer of the Staff and commander of the northern expedition against them.
value.literal: In Gaozu's time, when the Rouran violated the frontier, Cheng was added as Bearer of the Staff and commander of the armies for the northern campaign to attack them.

value.zh: 蠕蠕遁走，又以氐羌反叛，除都督梁益荊三州諸軍事、征南大將軍、梁州刺史。
value.en: The Rouran fled. Later, when the Di and Qiang rebelled, he was appointed commander of military affairs in Liang, Yi, and Jing provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the South, and inspector of Liang Province.
value.literal: The Rouran fled; later, when the Di and Qiang rebelled, he was appointed commander of military affairs in Liang, Yi, and Jing provinces, Grand General Who Conquers the South, and Inspector of Liang Province.

value.zh: 文明太后引見澄，誡厲之，顧謂中書令李沖曰：「此兒風神吐發，德音閑婉，當為宗室領袖。
value.en: Empress Dowager Wenming received Cheng, admonished him, then turned to Secretariat Director Li Chong. "This young man's bearing is splendid and his speech is gentle; he will become a leader of the imperial clan.
value.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming summoned Cheng, admonished him, and turned to Secretariat Director Li Chong, saying, "This child's bearing and expression are outstanding, and his words are gentle and refined; he will become a leader of the imperial clan.

value.zh: 是行使之必稱我意。
value.en: On this mission he will surely satisfy me.
value.literal: On this mission he will certainly satisfy my intent.

value.zh: 卿但記之，我不妄談人物也。」
value.en: Remember this: I do not misjudge men."
value.literal: You need only remember this; I do not speak of men falsely."

value.zh: 梁州氐帥楊仲顯、婆羅、楊卜兄弟及符叱盤等，自以居邊地險，世為山狡。
value.en: The Di leaders in Liang Province, including Yang Zhongxian, the brothers Poluo and Yang Bu, and Fu Chipan, trusted in the rugged frontier and had long lived as mountain raiders.
value.literal: The Di leaders of Liang Province, Yang Zhongxian, the brothers Poluo and Yang Bu, Fu Chipan, and others relied on living in dangerous borderlands and had for generations acted as mountain brigands.

value.zh: 澄至州，量彼風俗，誘導懷附。
value.en: When Cheng arrived, he studied their customs and coaxed them into allegiance.
value.literal: When Cheng reached the province, he assessed their customs and guided them into submission.

value.zh: 表送婆羅，授仲顯循城鎮副將，楊卜廣業太守，叱盤固道鎮副將，自餘首帥，各隨才而用之，款附者賞，違命加誅，於是仇池帖然，西南款順。
value.en: He sent Poluo to court, made Zhongxian deputy commander at Xuncheng, Yang Bu governor of Guangye, and Chipan deputy commander at Gudao, and used the other chiefs according to their abilities. Those who submitted were rewarded, those who resisted were punished; Qiuchi was pacified and the southwest came over.
value.literal: He memorialized to send Poluo to court, appointed Zhongxian deputy commander of Xuncheng Garrison, Yang Bu governor of Guangye, and Chipan deputy commander of Gudao Garrison; the remaining chiefs were each employed according to their talents. Those who sincerely submitted were rewarded, and those who disobeyed were punished. Thus Qiuchi became settled, and the southwest submitted.

value.zh: 加侍中，賜衣一襲、乘馬一匹，以旌其能。
value.en: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and given a set of robes and a riding horse in recognition of his skill.
value.literal: He was additionally made Palace Attendant and was granted one set of robes and one riding horse to commend his ability.

value.zh: 後轉征東大將軍、開府、徐州刺史，甚有聲績。
value.en: Later he became Grand General Who Conquers the East, opened his office, and served as inspector of Xu Province, earning a strong record of achievement.
value.literal: Later he was transferred as Grand General Who Conquers the East, opened his office, and served as Inspector of Xu Province, where he had a very strong reputation for achievement.

value.zh: 朝於京師，引見於皇信堂。
value.en: He came to the capital for court audience and was received in the Hall of Imperial Trust.
value.literal: He came to court at the capital and was received in the Hall of Imperial Trust.

value.zh: 高祖詔澄曰：「昔鄭子產鑄刑書，而晉叔向非之。
value.en: Gaozu asked Cheng, "When Zheng Zichan cast the penal code, Shu Xiang of Jin criticized him.
value.literal: Gaozu issued an edict to Cheng: "In former times Zheng Zichan cast the written laws, and Shu Xiang of Jin criticized him.

value.zh: 此二人皆是賢士，得失竟誰？」
value.en: Both were worthy men; in the end, who was right?"
value.literal: Both men were worthies; in the end, who was right and who was wrong?"

value.zh: 對曰：「鄭國寡弱，攝於強鄰，民情去就，非刑莫制，故鑄刑書以示威。
value.en: Cheng replied, "Zheng was weak and hemmed in by powerful neighbors. The people could not be controlled without punishments, so Zichan cast the laws to show authority.
value.literal: Cheng replied, "The state of Zheng was weak and constrained by powerful neighbors; the people's movements could not be controlled without punishments, so Zichan cast the written laws to display authority.

value.zh: 雖乖古式，合今權道，隨時濟世，子產為得。
value.en: Though it violated ancient form, it fit the needs of the moment. Zichan adapted to his age and helped the world, so he was right.
value.literal: Though this departed from ancient norms, it suited the expedient way of that time; he adapted to the age and aided the world, so Zichan was right.

value.zh: 而叔向譏議，示不忘古，可與論道，未可語權。」
value.en: Shu Xiang's criticism showed that he had not forgotten antiquity; one could discuss principle with him, but not expedience."
value.literal: Shu Xiang's criticism showed that he did not forget antiquity; one may discuss the Way with him, but not expediency."

value.zh: 高祖曰：「任城當欲為魏之子產也。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "Rencheng must wish to be Wei's Zichan."
value.literal: Gaozu said, "Rencheng must wish to be the Wei state's Zichan."

value.zh: 澄曰：「子產道合當時，聲流竹素。
value.en: Cheng replied, "Zichan's way suited his time, and his name passed into the histories.
value.literal: Cheng said, "Zichan's way matched his time, and his name was handed down in the bamboo and silk records.

value.zh: 臣既庸近，何敢庶幾。
value.en: I am mediocre and shallow. How could I dare compare myself to him?
value.literal: Your servant is mediocre and shallow; how would I dare hope to approach him?

value.zh: 今陛下以四海為家，宣文德以懷天下，但江外尚阻，車書未一，季世之民，易以威伏，難以禮治。
value.en: Your Majesty now makes the four seas your household and uses civil virtue to embrace the realm, but beyond the river resistance remains, and script and carriage tracks are not yet one. People in a late age are easy to subdue by force and hard to govern by ritual.
value.literal: Now Your Majesty has made the four seas your household and proclaims civil virtue to embrace the realm, but beyond the river there is still obstruction, and carriage tracks and writing have not yet been unified. People of a declining age are easy to subdue with authority and hard to govern by ritual.

value.zh: 愚謂子產之法，猶應暫用，大同之後，便以道化之。」
value.en: In my foolish view, Zichan's methods should still be used for a time; once unity is complete, then the Way can transform them."
value.literal: In my foolish view, Zichan's laws should still be used for a time; after great unity is achieved, then they may be transformed by the Way."

value.zh: 高祖心方革變，深善其對，笑曰：「非任城無以識變化之體。
value.en: Gaozu was then intent on reform, and he deeply approved Cheng's answer. Smiling, he said, "Without Rencheng, no one would understand the essence of transformation.
value.literal: Gaozu's mind was then set on reform and change, and he deeply approved Cheng's answer, smiling as he said, "Without Rencheng, no one could understand the substance of transformation.

value.zh: 朕方創改朝制，當與任城共萬世之功耳。」
value.en: I am just beginning to remake the court's institutions; Rencheng and I shall share in a work for ten thousand generations."
value.literal: I am now beginning to alter the institutions of the court and shall share with Rencheng a work for ten thousand generations."

value.zh: 後徵為中書令，改授尚書令。
value.en: Later Cheng was summoned as Director of the Secretariat and then made Director of the Masters of Writing.
value.literal: Later Cheng was summoned as Director of the Secretariat, then reassigned as Director of the Masters of Writing.

value.zh: 蕭賾使庾蓽來朝，蓽見澄音韻遒雅，風儀秀逸，謂主客郎張彝曰：「往魏任城以武著稱，今魏任城乃以文見美也。」
value.en: When Xiao Ze sent Yu Bi to court, Bi found Cheng's speech forceful and elegant and his bearing refined. He told Reception Gentleman Zhang Yi, "The former Rencheng of Wei was known for arms; this Rencheng of Wei is admired for culture."
value.literal: When Xiao Ze sent Yu Bi to court, Bi saw that Cheng's speech was strong and elegant and his bearing fine and graceful, and he told Reception Gentleman Zhang Yi, "In the past Wei's Rencheng was known for martial prowess; now Wei's Rencheng is admired for culture."

value.zh: 時詔延四廟之子，下逮玄孫之冑，申宗宴於皇信堂，不以爵秩為列，悉序昭穆為次，用家人之禮。
value.en: At that time the court invited the imperial kin, from sons of the four temples down to great-great-grandsons, to a clan banquet in the Hall of Imperial Trust. They were seated not by rank but by ancestral order, using the rites of one family.
value.literal: At the time an edict extended invitation from sons of the four temples down to descendants in the dark-garment generation, holding an imperial-clan banquet in the Hall of Imperial Trust. They were not arranged by noble rank, but all were ordered by Zhao and Mu seniority and treated with family rites.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「行禮已畢，欲令宗室各言其志，可率賦詩。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "The rites are finished. I want each kinsman to state his aspirations; let each compose a poem."
value.literal: Gaozu said, "The rites are complete; I wish each member of the imperial clan to speak his aspirations. You may all compose poems."

value.zh: 特令澄為七言連韻，與高祖往復賭賽，遂至極歡，際夜乃罷。
value.en: He specially ordered Cheng to compose linked seven-character rhymes. Cheng and Gaozu traded verses in playful contest until they were thoroughly delighted, stopping only late at night.
value.literal: He specifically ordered Cheng to compose linked seven-character rhymes, and he and Gaozu exchanged verses in contest until their joy became extreme; only when night had fallen did they stop.

value.zh: 後高祖外示南討，意在謀遷，齋於明堂左个，詔太常卿王諶，親令龜卜，易筮南伐之事，其兆遇革。
value.en: Later Gaozu publicly presented plans for a southern campaign, while actually planning the capital move. Fasting in the left chamber of the Mingtang, he had Grand Director of Ceremonies Wang Chen personally divine by turtle and milfoil about the campaign; the omen was Revolution.
value.literal: Later Gaozu outwardly displayed plans for a southern campaign, but his intention was to plan the move of the capital. Fasting in the left chamber of the Mingtang, he ordered Grand Director of Ceremonies Wang Chen to divine personally by turtle shell and milfoil about the southern campaign; the sign received was Revolution.

value.zh: 高祖曰：「此是湯武革命，順天應人之卦也。」
value.en: Gaozu said, "This is the hexagram by which Tang and Wu changed the mandate, obeying Heaven and answering the people."
value.literal: Gaozu said, "This is the hexagram by which Tang and Wu changed the mandate, following Heaven and responding to men."

value.zh: 羣臣莫敢言。
value.en: None of the ministers dared speak.
value.literal: None of the ministers dared speak.

value.zh: 澄進曰：「易言革者更也。
value.en: Cheng stepped forward. "In the Changes, Revolution means change.
value.literal: Cheng stepped forward and said, "In the Changes, ge means change.

value.zh: 將欲應天順人，革君臣之命，湯武得之為吉。
value.en: When Tang and Wu obeyed Heaven, answered the people, and changed the mandate between ruler and minister, this hexagram was auspicious.
value.literal: When one is about to accord with Heaven and respond to men and change the mandate between ruler and minister, Tang and Wu obtained it as auspicious.

value.zh: 階下帝有天下，重光累葉。
value.en: Your Majesty already possesses the realm, with shining succession through many generations.
value.literal: Your Majesty possesses the realm, and bright succession has continued through many generations.

value.zh: 今曰卜征，乃可伐叛，不得云革命。
value.en: Today the divination is for a campaign; it may mean attacking rebels, but it cannot mean changing the mandate.
value.literal: Today you call this a divination for campaign; it can mean suppressing rebels, but it cannot be called changing the mandate.

value.zh: 此非君人之卦，未可全為吉也。」
value.en: This is not the hexagram for a reigning lord, and it cannot be taken as wholly auspicious."
value.literal: This is not a hexagram for one who rules men, and it cannot be taken wholly as auspicious."

value.zh: 高祖厲聲曰：「象云『大人虎變』，何言不吉也！」
value.en: Gaozu said sternly, "The Image says, 'The great man changes like a tiger.' How can you say it is not auspicious?"
value.literal: Gaozu said in a stern voice, "The Image says, 'The great man changes like a tiger.' How can you say it is not auspicious?"

value.zh: 澄曰：「陛下龍興既久，豈可方同虎變！」
value.en: Cheng replied, "Your Majesty's dragon rise has long been established; how can it be compared to a tiger's change?"
value.literal: Cheng said, "Your Majesty's dragon rise has long endured; how can it be compared to the tiger's change?"

value.zh: 高祖勃然作色曰：「社稷我社稷，任城而欲沮眾也！」
value.en: Gaozu's face darkened. "The state is my state. Does Rencheng mean to obstruct everyone?"
value.literal: Gaozu suddenly changed color and said, "The altars of state are my altars of state; does Rencheng wish to obstruct the assembly?"

value.zh: 澄曰：「社稷誠知陛下之社稷，然臣是社稷之臣子，豫參顧問，敢盡愚衷。」
value.en: Cheng said, "I know well that the state is Your Majesty's, but I am its servant and son. Since I have been admitted to counsel, I dare give all my foolish sincerity."
value.literal: Cheng said, "I truly know the altars of state are Your Majesty's altars, yet I am a servant and son of the state. Since I have been allowed to join in consultation, I dare exhaust my foolish sincerity."

value.zh: 高祖既銳意必行，惡澄此對，久之乃解，曰：「各言其志，亦復何傷。」
value.en: Gaozu was determined to proceed and disliked Cheng's answer, but after a long while he relented. "Each has stated his mind; what harm is there?"
